task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Does a within-game change of the offensive five shift shot mix beyond what shooter identity alone explains?
Can the apparent shot-mix shift be separated from mechanical changes in who takes shots?
Are substitution-based contrasts confounded by game state, coach response, and fatigue?
Is the design powered for small shot-mix shifts given the available possession counts?
Are derived play-type labels reliable enough to serve as outcomes or controls?

historical_evidence.finding: PULL_UP exposure-effect diagnostics. With lineup fixed effects the slope holding shot fixed was -0.0255 (0.0061); without lineup FE it was -0.0063 (0.0036); placebo on other play types was -0.0075 (0.0017). [prior work] attributes the apparent effect to a shooter-level confound (failure mechanism C_artifact, limited by [prior work]; risks CONFOUNDING and PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE). Sample and power recorded as NOT_RECORDED.

Opponent lineup adaptation: shot mix when the opposing rim big is off the floor. Recorded results ([prior work] and [prior work]) include DRIVE +0.82pp (SE 0.25), POST_UP +0.43pp (SE 0.18), 3PA -1.79pp (SE 0.31), rim <=4ft +0.12pp (SE about 0.30), and PPP +0.008 (SE 0.007). [prior work]'s chat verdict is WEAK/SMALL and it is limited by [prior work] (risk SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER). [prior work] used N=1.07M possessions. This concerns the defensive side, not changes in the offensive five.

Defensive in-game adaptation to repeated play type (exposure slope). League-wide within-game slope was -0.0019 PPP per exposure (SE 0.0019); across-game +0.0004 (SE 0.0015). Only PULL_UP survived Holm (-0.0243, SE 0.0061, holm 0.0004). Team-trait split-half r was +0.008 and season-to-season r was +0.037. Limited by insufficient exposure, label or classification error, and low measurement reliability.

Observed on-ball defensive scheme labels (ORL-DET G1). Only 14.9% (DET, 10 of 67) and 3.3% (ORL, 2 of 60) of on-ball possessions received confident labels. The switches_on field was unpopulated in the NBA matchups feed. Verdict: failed_gate, limited by label error and small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing a play-type exposure decline to defensive adaptation, using lineup fixed effects and holding shot fixed
failed_approaches.why: The effect shrank from -0.0255 to -0.0063 when lineup FE were removed, and the same-shooter placebo on other play types was of similar size (-0.0075). [prior work] concludes shooter-level confounding (C_artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting sub-1pp shot-mix shifts from opposing-big absence
failed_approaches.why: Estimates were small and imprecise (rim share SE 0.295). The PPP effect had t=+1.1. [prior work]'s verdict is WEAK/SMALL and it will not carry a paper ([prior work]).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring within-game defensive adaptation to repeated play types
failed_approaches.why: Most play types gave near-zero slopes with wide intervals. Only PULL_UP survived correction, and its validity is undermined by the artifact finding in SF-[prior work]. Team-trait reliability was very low (split-half r +0.008).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball defensive coverage (DROP[path]) from the matchups feed
failed_approaches.why: Label rates were very low and switches_on was not populated, so the question was judged unanswerable with this data (A_unanswerable).

evidence_establishes: Shooter-level confounding can produce an apparent exposure or personnel effect that disappears or shrinks when shooter identity is controlled (SF-[prior work]). Any test of the offensive-five question must include a same-shooter placebo.
Effects of the size typical in this project's shot-mix work (sub-1pp to about 2pp) are hard to detect with the available sample unless the contrast is tightly designed ([prior work], [prior work]).

Derived defensive scheme labels are not reliable at usable rates from this feed (SF-[prior work]), so derived play-type or coverage labels should not serve as primary outcomes or controls without validation.
No retrieved record tests whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix. The question is therefore open.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix in these seasons. No retrieved record studies offensive-five changes as the exposure.
The size of any offensive-five effect, or whether the design has power for it. SF-[prior work] did not record sample and power, and [prior work] and [prior work] concern other exposures.
Whether the question's premise (that the design can detect personnel effects) holds. The question text presupposes the answer; the retrieved records do not verify it.
Whether substitution timing is exogenous to shot selection in these data. No record examined coach substitution decisions.
own_inferences: Shot mix will almost certainly change when the offensive five changes, because different players take different shots. This mechanical change is not evidence of a personnel effect. The informative estimand is the residual shot-mix change after conditioning on shooter identity and expected shot quality.

Because of this mechanical floor, the phrase 'showing the design can detect personnel effects' is nearly guaranteed by composition and would be a weak test. A valid design must show that the residual, shooter-adjusted shift is nonzero and that placebo contrasts are null.

Substitutions are chosen in response to game state (score, foul trouble, fatigue), so they are probably not random. Controlling for game state and using within-game contrasts with team-by-period fixed effects reduces this risk but does not remove it.

Play-type labels from [source] database are derived from play-by-play outcomes (points, initiator). Using them as outcomes or stratifiers risks outcome-derived labels and leakage, so shot-level fields from the play-by-play should be used directly.
The three seasons (2022-23 to 2024-25) probably differ in pace, rules, and roster construction, so season fixed effects or season-specific estimates are needed.
uncertainties: The retrieved records are about related but distinct questions. No record reports power, effect size, or sample size for offensive-five changes.
Sample sizes for qualifying substitution contrasts are unknown until counted in the data.
The [prior work] record is truncated in the retrieval ('[cut; read_family for the full text]'). Its PULL_UP detail was not read in full.
The 'auto_' fields in [prior work] are system-generated classifications; I have reported them as recorded and have not independently verified them.
Whether the substitution_rotation intervals and starters files align exactly with play-by-play clocks is not established by any record.

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval, the plan looked like a standard within-game substitution contrast. The retrieved records changed it in three ways. (1) SF-[prior work] showed that shooter-level confounding can create an apparent personnel-linked effect, so the design must hold shooter identity fixed and include same-shooter placebo outcomes. (2) [prior work] and [prior work] showed that small shot-mix effects are underpowered here, so the design needs a pre-specified minimum detectable effect and a restricted, high-exposure sample. (3) SF-[prior work] showed that derived labels are unreliable, so the outcome must come from raw shot-level fields. These changes mean the question should proceed only as a restricted, pre-registered test, not as a general claim.

blocking_constraints.text: Shot mix changes mechanically when shooters change. Without conditioning on shooter identity and expected shot quality, a detected shift would be uninformative about personnel effects.
Substitutions respond to game state and fatigue. Within-game contrasts with game-state controls are needed, and residual confounding remains possible.
Prior shot-mix effects of sub-1pp to about 2pp were underpowered or weak ([prior work], [prior work]). A minimum detectable effect must be computed before analysis.
Derived play-type and coverage labels are unreliable (SF-[prior work]) and may be built from outcomes. Primary outcomes must use raw shot-level fields.

prior_work.summary: None of the retrieved records tests whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix. [prior work] and [prior work] address defensive-side and exposure questions and are related only in method. SF-[prior work] is the most relevant methodological warning (shooter-level confound). SF-[prior work] is relevant to label reliability. The question is therefore not already answered by retrieved work.

risks.text: Different shooters take different shots, so shot mix shifts by construction. A positive result without shooter-level adjustment is not evidence of a personnel effect.
Coach substitution decisions depend on score, foul trouble, and fatigue, which also affect shot selection.
The SF-[prior work] artifact shows that a same-shooter placebo can reveal confounding. A null placebo is required before a positive effect is interpreted.
Substitutions may follow short-term performance or shot results, producing regression-to-the-mean effects on shot mix.
Effects of the magnitude seen in [prior work] and [prior work] may be too small for the available swap count, especially after restricting to qualifying contrasts.
Many offensive-five changes involve few possessions, and shot-type cells (3PA, rim, post) are sparse within a single stint.
Team and season trait reliability was very low in [prior work] (r about 0.01 to 0.04), so team-level shot-mix tendencies may be unstable outcomes.
Play-type labels derived from [source] database may encode points or shot outcomes, which would leak the outcome into the predictor or stratifier.
Defensive scheme labels were largely unpopulated (SF-[prior work]). Any matchup-based control is unreliable without validation.
Shot-mix tendencies and substitution patterns may shift across 2022-23 to 2024-25, and playoff rotations differ from regular season.
Multiple shot zones, substitution types, and seasons create many comparisons, raising false-positive risk.
Alignment of substitution intervals, starters, and play-by-play clocks can introduce misattributed possessions.

design.estimand: Within-team change in offensive shot-zone distribution (rim, midrange, 3PA share, and expected points per shot) when one offensive player is replaced by another, conditional on shooter identity and expected shot quality, relative to placebo contrasts.
design.unit: Offensive possession, nested in team-game-stint. Contrasts are the 5 possessions before and after a single-player offensive substitution within the same game and period.
design.sample: Regular-season 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 play-by-play for all teams. Playoffs are excluded from the primary analysis and reserved as a secondary replication. Include only swaps where the entering and exiting players each have a minimum shot count, set in advance.
design.power: Before analysis, simulate the minimum detectable shot-mix shift at 80% power for the qualifying swap count. Report it and treat results below it as uncertain, not null. No power has been established by the retrieved records.
design.controls: Shooter identity fixed effects (run with and without, reporting both). Game-state controls: score margin, period, and clock bins. Team-by-period and season fixed effects. Minutes on floor as a fatigue proxy. Outcomes are raw shot-level fields from play-by-play, not derived play-type labels.
design.falsification: Placebo 1: the same swap contrasts with the outcome replaced by defensive-side shot mix, which should show no offensive personnel effect. Placebo 2: the same-shooter contrast on non-shot possessions (for example turnovers or fouls drawn). Placebo 3: pre-period contrasts (5 possessions before the swap compared with 5 possessions earlier), which should be null. If placebos are nonnull, the primary effect is treated as an artifact.
design.multiplicity: One primary test (shooter-adjusted residual shot mix, 3PA share). Secondary zones and playoff replication are reported under Holm correction across the pre-registered set.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the shooter-adjusted primary estimate has a 95% CI excluding zero, exceeds the pre-registered minimum detectable effect, and all three placebos are null with CIs including zero. Artifact if the effect is nonnull only without shooter FE, as in SF-[prior work]. Uncertain if power is below the threshold. Rejected only if powered and the primary and placebo estimates are null.
design.data_version: NBA regular-season play-by-play, substitution rotation intervals, starters, and box scores for 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25, as extracted on the pre-registration date (2026-11-02). Derived play-type graph labels are excluded from the primary analysis.
